title: Choose generic type parameters, constraints and variance markings without replacing type safety with object casts

questions.model:
`in`

Optional explanation: the declaration becomes `interface IHandler<in T>`. `T` appears only as an input, so a handler that accepts any `object` can safely accept a `string`.

questions.prompt:
A C# utility method must return the larger of two values of the same type. It is called with `int` values and with `string` values. The body compares the values with `a.CompareTo(b)`. The method must not take `object` parameters or use casts.

Write the method's signature, including any type parameter and constraint it needs.

rubric.point: Declares a generic type parameter that is used for both parameters and the return type, for example `static T Max<T>(T a, T b)`.
Adds a constraint that guarantees `CompareTo` on `T`, such as `where T : IComparable<T>` (non-generic `IComparable` is also accepted if `CompareTo` is called correctly).

questions.model:
```csharp
static T Max<T>(T a, T b) where T : IComparable<T>
```

Optional: without the constraint, an unconstrained `T` only exposes members that every type has, so `CompareTo` would not compile.

c2.text: public T CompareValues (T a, T b) where T : int, string

annotations.note: You chose `in`, contravariance. `T` is only an input, so an `IHandler<object>` can safely be used as an `IHandler<string>`.

c1.feedback: Correct: `in` makes `IHandler<T>` contravariant, so the assignment compiles.

annotations.quote: public T CompareValues (T a, T b)
annotations.note: The method has no type parameter list, so `T` is undefined and this does not compile. It needs `<T>` after the name, as in `CompareValues<T>`.
A constraint cannot name `int` or `string`, and no type can be both. The constraint has to be an interface such as `IComparable<T>`, which both types implement and which provides `CompareTo`.

c2.feedback: You had the right idea of a generic method with a constraint, but you left out `<T>` and listed concrete types instead of a constraint interface like `IComparable<T>`.
